text:
Sam (Sales): Heads-up — FinCorp is asking for a tight POC: EU-only data residency + byok KMS and no non-EU subprocessors in the request path. Can we do that for a 2-week pilot?
Priya (SE): Quick clarifying q: when they say 'no non-EU subprocessors' do they mean control plane, data plane, or both?
Sam (Sales): They said all data plane processing must remain in EU. Control plane signaling is ok if metadata only. Customer legal wants proof of subprocessor list for any infra that touches requests.
Tomas (Ops): Technically we can pin tenant to eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 pools for the POC. Need to check model availability & quantized variants there. Also BYOK: we have KMS integrations in eu-west-1 for primary cloud provider, but HSM/BYO-HSM is a longer lift.
Elaine (Security): Attach SCQ (security questionnaire) answers in the thread? They asked about subprocessors + transfer risk. We should provide the subprocessors inventory + an attestation for the POC window.
Ben (Pricing): Note: regional pinning + BYOK adds a ~30% infra uplift estimate for reserved pool — because we may have to reserve GPUs in EU instead of multi-region burst capacity. Need to confirm exact numbers.
Priya (SE): For the POC scope I propose: 1) tenant pin to eu-west-1; 2) BYOK via our KMS connector (customer supplies key ARN); 3) explicit subprocessor list snapshot for the POC dates; 4) fail-open policy? They want no cross-border failover unless pre-approved.
Tomas (Ops): Implementation notes:
```
- create tenant config: residency=EU
- model_variant: r-instruct-7b-quant (eu pool)
- kms: external-key-arn -> map to customer KEK
- routing: strict_pin=true, fallback=notify_only
```
Tomas (Ops): If strict_pin=true then autoscaling/bursting is constrained to the EU pool; if capacity exhausted we'll queue or return 429s unless we implement an approved manual failover.
Sam (Sales): Customer will accept queued requests during the POC, but wants a documented escalation path if latency > 2s p50 for inference.
Elaine (Security): For the SCQ & legal: I can generate a POC attestation stating subprocessors for the POC date range and that no logs or model payloads will leave EU. Need ops confirmation on logging endpoints (metrics/trace exporters).
Tomas (Ops): Logging: trace sampling currently goes to our observability plane (multi-region). We can switch to EU-only retention & export for this tenant for POC — will need a small runtime config change.
Ben (Pricing): I'll draft a POC cost estimate: reserved pool hours + BYOK connector + eng support hours (oncall coverage). Rough ballpark: €8k–€12k for two weeks.
Priya (SE): Also flag: some smaller model variants aren’t present in EU pools yet; fallback model families exist but may change latency/quality. We'll include simple eval prompts so FinCorp can see differences.
Sam (Sales): Action items: @Priya please draft the technical POC checklist + sample config. @Tomas confirm we can switch traces/logs to EU-only and add ops steps. @Elaine produce attestation + SCQ answers. @Ben send estimate and note SLA implications. I’ll loop FinCorp in once we have the packet.
Ben (Pricing): Will send estimate by EOD.
Priya (SE): Draft attached (high level):
- POC duration: 2 weeks
- Traffic target: 5k req/day, 95th latency target < 1.5s
- Residency: tenant pinned to eu-west-1; no data plane egress outside EU
- BYOK: customer-managed key ARN, rotated per agreement
- Subprocessors snapshot: infra (eu cloud provider), monitoring (EU-only endpoint for POC), storage (EU region)
- Failure mode: queue + notify; manual failover only with signed approval

Elaine (Security): I'll need the subprocessors list from ops to verify. Once I sign off I'll include the attestation PDF and the SCQ sheet.
Tomas (Ops): Confirmed: we can produce a subprocessors snapshot for the POC run dates and flip observability exports to EU-only. I'll schedule a short maintenance window for config push (low risk).
infra-bot: deploy requested: apply residency-pin for tenant fincorp-poc -> queued (CI job 8923).
Sam (Sales): Great. Target to get packet to customer tomorrow morning. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Priya (SE): I'll also prepare a short eval report template so they can validate quality regressions between EU and default variants.
Ben (Pricing): Estimate posted in internal quote doc, linking now: https://redwood.internal/quotes/POC-1754286011
Elaine (Security): One more ask from legal: add wording that during POC we won't schedule cross-border failover without 24h notice. Will add to attestation.
Tomas (Ops): Noted. I'll include the maintenance/failover playbook with contact list.
Sam (Sales): Awesome — will close loop with FinCorp after docs ready.
